cases.title: Counterfactual Baseline
cases.long_description: Baseline assumptions for economic growth, oil prices, oil and gas supplies, and zero-carbon technology costs.

cases.title: High Economic Growth
cases.long_description: Case developed to reflect the uncertainty in projections of economic growth. In the high economic growth case, real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 2.2 percent from 2025 to 2050.

cases.title: Low Economic Growth
cases.long_description: Case developed to reflect the uncertainty in projections of economic growth. In the low economic growth case, real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 1.2 percent from 2025 to 2050.

cases.title: High Oil and Gas Supply
cases.long_description: Oil and gas supply cases examine the uncertainty with respect to the cost and availability of domestic resources on energy supply, demand, trade, and prices. In the High Oil and Gas supply case, the estimated ultimate recovery per well for tight oil, tight gas, or shale gas in the United States and undiscovered resources in Alaska and the offshore Lower 48 states is assumed to be 50% higher than in the Counterfactual Baseline case. Rates of technological improvement that reduce costs and increase productivity in the United States are also 50% higher than in the Counterfactual Baseline case.

cases.title: Low Oil and Gas Supply
cases.long_description: Oil and gas supply cases examine the uncertainty with respect to the cost and availability of domestic resources on energy supply, demand, trade, and prices. In the Low Oil and Gas supply case, the estimated ultimate recovery per well for tight oil, tight gas, or shale gas in the United States and undiscovered resources in Alaska and the offshore Lower 48 states is assumed to be 50% lower than in the Counterfactual Baseline case. Rates of technological improvement that reduce costs and increase productivity in the United States are also 50% lower than in the Counterfactual Baseline case.

cases.title: High Zero-Carbon Technology Cost
cases.long_description: High Zero-Carbon Technology Cost case assumes no capital cost reductions from learning by doing compared with the Counterfactual Baseline case for zero-emission technologies. Technologies include renewables, nuclear, and diurnal storage in the power sector, solar PV and wind in the end-use sector, and electrolyzer for hydrogen production.

cases.title: Low Zero-Carbon Technology Cost
cases.long_description: Low Zero-Carbon Technology Cost case assumes faster cost reduction from learning by doing compared with the Counterfactual Baseline case for zero-emission technologies. Technologies include renewables, nuclear, and diurnal storage in the power sector, solar PV and wind in the end-use sector, and electrolyzer for hydrogen production.

cases.title: Alternative Electricity
cases.long_description: Alternative Electricity case assumes that the Federal greenhouse gas emissions standards for the power sector under Section 111 of the CAA are not in place.

cases.title: Alternative Transportation
cases.long_description: The Alternative Transportation case assumes the following policies are not in place: 1) for light-duty vehicles, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards and EPA's vehicle tailpipe emission standards for model years 2027 and later; 2) for trucks and buses, the EPA Phase 3 tailpipe emissions standards for model years 2027 and later; and 3) for trucks and buses, the EPA Low NOx standards for model years 2027 and later. Rules affecting fuel economy and tailpipe emissions that were issued for model years 2026 and earlier remain in place. Removal of the most recent tailpipe standards required adjustments to assumptions regarding vehicle manufacturer product plans and the anticipated rollout of charging infrastructure.

cases.title: Alternative Electricity and Transportation
cases.long_description: Includes assumptions for the power sector as defined in the Alternative Electricity case and assumptions for the transportation sector as defined in the Alternative Transportation case.

cases.title: High Electricity Demand
cases.long_description: High Electricity Demand case examines uncertainty about long-term computational requirements and data center server power draw across the commercial building stock. We assume growth in the installed stock of AI servers follows an exponential trend through 2050 and electricity used to support data centers is more intensive than we assume in our Counterfactual Baseline case.

Liquids supply is lower due to a lack of global investment in the oil sector.  Brent spot price rises to $170 per barrel (2021 dollars) in 2050.

cases.title: Low price
cases.long_description: Oil price case to illustrate potential variation in global demand for and supply of petroleum and other liquid fuels. The low oil price case assumes conditions under which global (excluding the United States) liquids demand is lower and supply is higher than in the Reference case.  The conditions supporting this scenario include slowed economic growth, reduced consumption due to more efficient technologies, and industrial fuel switching from liquids to natural gas feedstocks. Brent spot price falls to $44 per barrel (2021 dollars) in 2050.

cases.title: High oil and gas supply
cases.long_description: Oil and gas supply case to examine the effects of domestic supply on energy demand, imports, and prices.  In the high oil and gas supply case, the estimated ultimate recovery per well for tight oil, tight gas, or shale gas in the United States and undiscovered resources in Alaska and the offshore Lower 48 states is assumed to be 50% higher than in the Reference case. Rates of technological improvement that reduce costs and increase productivity in the United States are also 50% higher than in the Reference case. In addition, tight oil and shale gas resources are added to reflect new plays or the expansion of known plays.

cases.title: Low oil and gas supply
cases.long_description: Oil and gas supply case to examine the effects of domestic supply on energy demand, imports, and prices.  In the low oil and gas supply case, the estimated ultimate recovery per well for tight oil, tight gas, or shale gas in the United States and undiscovered resources in Alaska and the offshore Lower 48 states is assumed to be 50% lower than in the Reference case. Rates of technological improvement that reduce costs and increase productivity in the United States are also 50% lower than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High renewable cost
cases.long_description: Renewables cost case introduced to address uncertainty in future costs of renewable power generation technologies.  In the high renewables cost case, the overnight capital cost is held constant at the 2021 level throughout the projection period for all renewable technologies, including conventional hydropower, in the electric power sector and for small wind and solar technologies in the end-use sectors.

cases.title: Low renewable cost
cases.long_description: Renewables cost case introduced to address uncertainty in future costs of renewable power generation technologies. In the low renewables cost case, overnight capital costs, operating and maintenance costs, and fuel prices, where applicable, are assumed to decline more rapidly than in the Reference case, reaching levels 40% below their Reference case equivalents by 2050 for all renewable generation technologies (wind, solar, conventional hydropower, biomass, geothermal, and municipal solid waste), including in end-use applications.

cases.title: No Interstate Pipeline Builds

cases.title: AWA - 10-year Historical Trend

cases.title: AWA - Rate Change: Cooler

cases.title: AWA - Rate Change: Warmer

cases.title: Low renewable cost

cases.title: No ACE

cases.title: Low price

subjects.name: Liquids and Natural Gas Supply and Prices
Regional Details in a Single Table

cases.title: Reference
cases.long_description: Baseline assumptions for economic growth (2.4 percent from 2013 through 2040), oil prices, and technology.  Brent spot price rises to about $141.30 per barrel (2013 dollars) in 2040.

cases.title: Policy
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan with the EPA proposed carbon intensity targets during the interim and final compliance periods, enforced at the NEMS Electricity Market Module region level.  Choice of heat rate improvements (HRI) based on the representation of the cost and degree of potential HRI incorporated in the current (AEO2015) version of NEMS.  Re-dispatch of affected electric generating units as an available compliance strategy.  Credit in compliance calculations for generation from existing and new renewable capacity.  Credit in compliance calculations for currently under-construction nuclear capacity and 6% of generation from existing nuclear capacity.  Expansion of new low- and zero-carbon emitting generating capacity, including representation of state renewable portfolio standards.  Credit in compliance calculations for avoided generation as a result of incremental demand-side energy efficiency savings achieved through energy efficiency measures in the residential and commercial sectors.  A phased-in 2020-29 compliance trajectory, to reflect that the proposed rule allows states flexibility to determine their pre-2030 trajectory, if they meet interim targets on a 10-year average or cumulative basis

cases.title: Policy extension
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan extending carbon dioxide reduction targets beyond 2030, in order to reduce carbon dioxide emissions from the power sector by 45% below 2005 levels in 2040.

cases.title: Policy new nuclear
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan assuming that generation from currently unplanned new nuclear capacity counts in compliance calculations.

cases.title: High growth
cases.long_description: Real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 2.9 percent from 2013 to 2040.

cases.title: Policy high growth
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan with real GDP growing at an average annual rate of 2.9 percent from 2013 to 2040.

cases.title: High resource
cases.long_description: Estimated ultimate recovery per shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well is 50% higher and well spacing is 50% closer (or the number of wells left to be drilled is 100% higher) than in the Reference case.  In addition, tight oil resources are added to reflect new plays or the expansion of known tight oil plays, and the estimated ultimate recovery for tight and shale wells increases by 1% per year more than the annual increase in the Reference case to reflect additional technology improvements.  Also includes kerogen development; and undiscovered resources in the lower 48 offshore and Alaska, and shale gas and coalbed resources in Canada that are 50% higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Policy high resource
cases.description: Policy with high oil and gas resource
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan with estimated ultimate recovery per shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well is 50% higher and well spacing is 50% closer (or the number of wells left to be drilled is 100% higher) than in the Reference case.  In addition, tight oil resources are added to reflect new plays or the expansion of known tight oil plays, and the estimated ultimate recovery for tight and shale wells increases by 1% per year more than the annual increase in the Reference case to reflect additional technology improvements.  Also includes kerogen development; and undiscovered resources in the lower 48 offshore and Alaska, and shale gas and coalbed resources in Canada that are 50% higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Policy biomass CO2
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan assuming that the emission rate for biomass fuel is 195 pounds carbon dioxide per million Btu, as assumed by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency in its Regulatory Impact Analysis, in place of the U.S. Energy Information Administration’s Reference case assumption that biomass is carbon neutral.

cases.title: Policy phase-in
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan assuming the state phase-in paths from Appendix 1 of EPA’s Goal Computation Technical Support Document (TSD), without modification. These phase-in paths tend to represent larger reductions in the early compliance years, compared to the phase-in paths assumed in the bulk of this analysis.

cases.title: Policy with no EOR
cases.description: Policy with no enhanced oil recovery
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan assuming no market for CO2 from the electric power sector for enhanced oil recovery purposes.

cases.title: Policy with national cooperation
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan assuming that Electricity Market Module regions group together to form a compliance region consisting of the entire lower-48 states, in order to analyze the impacts of wider regional compliance.

cases.title: Policy with limited trade
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan constraining transmission capacity between regions, resulting in a scenario that limits increases in interregional flows as a compliance strategy to meet Clean Power Plan requirements.

cases.title: Policy with no efficiency
cases.description: Policy with no demand side energy efficiency compliance
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan assuming that energy efficiency is not used as a compliance mechanism, without modification to state emission performance goals.

cases.title: Policy with high efficiency
cases.description: Policy with high demand side energy efficiency compliance
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan assuming that demand-side energy efficiency is subsidized more heavily relative to the Base Policy case.

cases.title: High HRI
cases.long_description: Baseline assumptions assuming maximum levels of heat rate improvement potential and associated cost.

cases.title: Policy with high HRI
cases.description: Policy with high heat rate improvement
cases.long_description: The proposed Clean Power Plan assuming the maximum levels of heat rate improvement potential and associated cost.

cases.title: Low HRI
cases.long_description: Baseline assumptions assuming minimum levels of heat rate improvement potential and associated cost.

cases.title: Policy with low HRI
cases.description: Policy with low heat rate improvement

cases.long_description: Combines the assumptions in the Accelerated Nuclear Retirements and Accelerated Coal Retirements cases.

cases.title: Low nuclear
cases.long_description: Begins with the Accelerated Nuclear Retirements case and adds the assumptions in the High Oil and Gas Resource and the No Sunset cases.

cases.title: ESICA
cases.long_description: Assumes passage of the energy efficiency provisions in S. 1392 including appropriation of funds at the levels authorized in the bill. Key provisions modeled include improved national building codes for new homes and commercial buildings, and a rebate program for advanced industrial motor systems, assuming bill passage in 2014.  For new residential construction, building shell efficiencies are assumed to improve 15% relative to IECC2009 by 2020 and building code compliance is assumed to improve. New commercial building shells are assumed to be 30% more efficient than ASHRAE 90.1-2004 by 2020.

cases.title: Low coal cost
cases.long_description: Regional productivity growth rates for coal mining are approximately 2.4% per year higher than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment, and coal transportation rates are lower than in the Reference case, falling to about 25% below the Reference case in 2040. The price change for non-U.S. export supplies is assumed to be roughly 10% less than the price change projected for U.S. coal exports.

cases.title: High coal cost
cases.long_description: Regional productivity growth rates for coal mining are approximately 2.4% per year lower than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment, and coal transportation rates are higher than in the Reference case, ranging between 24 and 31% above the Reference case in 2040. The price change for non-U.S. export supplies is assumed to be roughly 10% less than the price change projected for U.S. coal exports.

cases.title: Low cost renewable
cases.long_description: Capital costs for new non-hydro renewable generating technologies are 20% lower than Reference case levels through 2040, and biomass feedstocks are 20% less expensive for a given resource quantity. Capital costs for new ethanol, biodiesel, pyrolysis, and other BTL production technologies are 20 percent lower than Reference case levels through 2040, and the industrial sector assumes a higher rate of recovery for biomass byproducts from industrial processes.

cases.title: Low resource
cases.long_description: Estimated ultimate recovery per shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well is 50% lower than in the Reference case. All other resource assumptions will remain the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: High resource
cases.long_description: Estimated ultimate recovery per shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well is 50% higher and well spacing is 50% lower (or the number of wells left to be drilled is 100% higher) than in the Reference case.  In addition, tight oil resources are added to reflect new plays or the expansion of known tight oil plays and the estimated ultimate recovery for tight and shale wells is increased 1% per year to reflect additional technological improvement.  Also includes kerogen development, tight oil resources in Alaska, and 50% higher undiscovered resources in lower 48 offshore and Alaska than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High VMT
cases.long_description: Assumes higher licensing rates and travel demand for specific age and gender cohorts.  Vehicle miles traveled per licensed driver is 3 percent higher than the Reference case in 2012, increases up to 7 percent by 2027, then declines to 3 percent above the Reference case by 2040.

cases.title: Low VMT
cases.long_description: Assumes lower licensing rates and travel demand for specific age and gender cohorts.  Vehicle miles traveled per licensed driver is 5 percent lower than the Reference case for the full projection.  Licensing rates stay constant at 2011 levels or decline from 2011 to 2040, specific to gender, age, and census division categories.

cases.title: High rail LNG
cases.long_description: Assumes a higher LNG locomotive penetration rate into motive stock such that 100 percent of locomotives are LNG capable by 2037.

cases.title: Low rail LNG
cases.long_description: Assumes a lower LNG locomotive penetration rate into motive stock, at a 1.0 average annual turnover rate for dual-fuel engines that can use up to 80 percent LNG.

cases.title: 2013 technology
cases.long_description: Assumes that future equipment purchases in the residential and commercial sectors are based only on the range of equipment available in 2013. Commercial and existing residential building shell efficiency is held constant at 2013 levels. Energy efficiency of new industrial plant and equipment is held constant at the 2014 level over the projection period.

cases.title: High technology
cases.long_description: Assumes earlier availability, lower costs, and higher efficiencies for more advanced residential and commercial equipment. For new residential construction, building code compliance is assumed to improve after 2013 and building shell efficiencies are assumed to meet ENERGY STAR requirements by 2023. Existing residential shell exhibits 50 percent more improvement than the Reference case after 2013. New and existing commercial building shells are assumed to improve 25 percent more than in the Reference case by 2040. Industrial sector assumes earlier availability, lower costs, and higher efficiency for more advanced equipment and a more rapid rate of improvement in the recovery of biomass byproducts from industrial processes. In the transportation sector, the characteristics of conventional and alternative-fuel LDVs reflect more optimistic assumptions about incremental improvements in fuel economy and costs, as well as battery electric vehicle costs. Freight trucks are assumed to see more rapid improvement in fuel efficiency.. More optimistic assumptions for fuel efficiency improvements are also made for the air, rail, and shipping sectors.

cases.title: Best available technology
cases.long_description: Assumes that all future equipment purchases in the residential and commercial sectors are made from a menu of technologies that includes only the most efficient models available in a particular year, regardless of cost. Residential building shells for new construction are all assumed to be code compliant and built to the most efficient specifications after 2013, and existing residential shells have twice the improvement of the Reference case. New and existing commercial building shell efficiencies improve 50 percent more than in the Reference case by 2040. Industrial and transportation sector assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: No GHG concern
cases.long_description: No greenhouse gas emissions reduction policy is enacted and market investment decisions are not altered in anticipation of such a policy.

cases.title: GHG10
cases.long_description: Applies a price for carbon dioxide emissions throughout the economy, starting at $10 per metric ton in 2015 and rising by 5 percent per year through 2040.

cases.title: GHG25
cases.long_description: Applies a price for carbon dioxide emissions throughout the economy, starting at $25 per metric ton in 2015 and rising by 5 percent per year through 2040.

cases.title: GHG10 with low gas price
cases.description: Greenhouse gas $10 and low gas prices
cases.long_description: Applies a price for carbon dioxide emissions throughout the economy, starting at $10 per metric ton in 2015 and rising by 5 percent per year through 2040.  Estimated ultimate recovery per shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well is 50% higher and well spacing is 50% lower (or the number of wells left to be drilled is 100% higher) than in the Reference case.  In addition, tight oil resources are added to reflect new plays or the expansion of known tight oil plays and the estimated ultimate recovery for tight and shale wells is increased 1% per year to reflect additional technological improvement.  Also includes kerogen development, tight oil resources in Alaska, and 50% higher undiscovered resources in lower 48 offshore and Alaska than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low electricity demand

Residential building shells for new construction are all assumed to be code compliant and built to the most efficient specifications after 2013, and existing residential shells have twice the improvement of the Reference case. New and existing commercial building shell efficiencies improve 50 percent more than in the Reference case by 2040. Industrial and transportation sector assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.] and also assumes greater improvement in industrial motor efficiency.

cases.title: Reference
cases.long_description: Baseline assumptions for economic growth (2.5 percent from 2011 through 2040), oil prices, and technology.  Brent spot price rises to about $163 per barrel (2011 dollars) in 2040.

cases.title: High growth
cases.long_description: Real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 2.9 percent from 2011 to 2040.

cases.title: Low growth
cases.long_description: Real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 1.9 percent from 2011 to 2040.

cases.title: High price
cases.long_description: High prices result from a combination of higher demand for petroleum and other liquids in the non-OECD nations and lower global supply.  Higher demand is measured by higher economic growth relative to the Reference case, with GDP growth in the non-OECD region being 0.6 percent higher on average in each projection year beginning in 2013.  Non-OPEC petroleum production expands more slowly in the short to middle term relative to the Reference case.  Brent spot price rises to $237 per barrel (2011 dollars) in 2040.

cases.title: Low price
cases.long_description: Low prices result from a combination of lower demand for petroleum and other liquids in the non-OECD nations and higher global supply.  Lower demand is measured by lower economic growth relative to the Reference case, with GDP growth in the non-OECD region being 1.1 percent lower on average in each projection year beginning in 2013.  OPEC increases its market share to 43 percent, and the costs of other liquid production technologies are lower than in the Reference case.  Brent spot price falls to $75 per barrel (2011 dollars) in 2040.

cases.title: Extended policies
cases.long_description: Extension of all existing energy policies and legislation that contains sunset provisions, including additional rounds of efficiency standards for residential and commercial products, as well as new standards for products not yet covered.  Adds multiple rounds of national building codes by 2026 and increases light-duty vehicle fuel economy standards in the transportation sector to 57.7 miles per gallon in 2040.  Increased capacity limitations on the renewable investment tax credit and extension of the program.

cases.title: No sunset
cases.long_description: Extension of all existing energy policies and legislation that contains sunset provisions, except those requiring additional funding (e.g., loan guarantee programs) and those that involve extensive regulatory analysis, such as CAFE improvements and periodic updates of efficiency standards.

cases.title: Low nuclear
cases.long_description: All nuclear plants are limited to a 60-year life (45 gigawatts of retirements), uprates are limited to the 1.3 gigawatts that have been reported to EIA, and planned additions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: High nuclear
cases.long_description: All nuclear plants are life-extended beyond 60 years (except for one announced retirement), and uprates are the same as in the Reference case  New plants include those under construction and plants that have a scheduled U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission or Atomic Safety and Licensing Board hearing.

cases.title: Small modular reactor
cases.long_description: Characteristics of the new advanced nuclear technology are based on a small modular design rather than the AP1000.

cases.title: Low coal cost
cases.long_description: Regional productivity growth rates for coal mining are approximately 2.5 percent per year higher than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment, and coal transportation rates in 2040 are about 25 percent lower than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High coal cost
cases.long_description: Regional productivity growth rates for coal mining are approximately 2.5 percent per year lower than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment, and coal transportation rates in 2040 are between 25 and 32 percent higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low cost renewable
cases.long_description: Costs for new nonhydropower renewable generating technologies are 20 percent lower than the Reference case levels through 2040.  Capital costs for new biomass-to-liquids technologies and biodiesel production technologies are reduced by 20 percent relative to the Reference case through 2040.

cases.title: Low resource
cases.long_description: Estimated ultimate recovery per shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well is 50 percent lower than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High resource
cases.long_description: Shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well estimated ultimate recoveries are 100 percent higher than in the Reference case and the maximum well spacing is assumed to be 40 acres.  Also includes kerogen development, tight oil resources in Alaska, and 50 percent higher undiscovered resources in lower 48 offshore and Alaska than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low import
cases.long_description: Greater improvement in vehicle efficiency and lower vehicle technology costs; a post-2025 increase in CAFE standards by 1.4 percent through 2040; lower vehicle miles traveled; expanded market availability of liquefied/compressed natural gas in heavy-duty trucks, rail, and marine; higher gas-to-liquids market penetration; optimistic batteryassumptions for electric drivetrain vehicle costs; increased market penetration of biomass pyrolysis oils, coal-to-liquids, and biomass-to-liquids; and more optimistic assumptions associated with E85 availability and maximum penetration of E15.  Shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well estimated ultimate recoveries are 100 percent higher than in the Reference case and the maximum well spacing is assumed to be 40 acres.  Also includes kerogen development, tight oil resources in Alaska, and 50 percent higher undiscovered resources in lower 48 offshore and Alaska than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High import
cases.long_description: Lower improvement in vehicle efficiency (driven by limits on technology improvement and nonenforcement of CAFE standards), higher vehicle miles traveled, no change in liquefied/compressed natural gas market availability, no change in gas-to-liquids penetration, no change in biofuel market penertration from the Reference case.  Estimated ultimate recovery per shale gas, tight gas, and tight oil well is 50 percent lower than in the Reference case.

cases.title: 2012 technology
cases.long_description: Future equipment purchases in the residential and commercial sectors are based only on the range of equipment available in 2012.  Building shell efficiency is held constant at 2012 levels.  Energy efficiency of new industrial plants and equipment is held constant at the 2013 level.

cases.title: High technology
cases.long_description: Earlier availability, lower costs, and higher efficiencies for more advanced residential and commercial equipment.  For new residential construction, building shell efficiencies are assumed to meet ENERGY STAR requirements after 2016.  Existing residential shell exhibits 50 percent more improvement than in the Reference case after 2012.  New and existing commercial building shells are assumed to improve 25 percent more than in the Reference case by 2040.  Earlier availability, lower costs, and higher efficiency is assumed for more advanced industrial equipment, and industrial processes exhibit a more rapid rate of improvement in the recovery of biomass byproducts from industrial processes.  Characteristics of conventional and alternative-fueled light-duty vehicles reflect more optimistic assumptions about incremental improvements in fuel economy and costs.  Freight trucks see more rapid improvement in fuel efficiency for engine and emission control technologies.  Fuel efficiency assumptions are more optimistic for the air, rail, and shipping sectors.

cases.title: Best available technology

Residential building shells for new construction are built to the most efficient specifications after 2012, and existing residential shells have twice the improvement of the Reference case. cases.long_description: Regional productivity growth rates for coal mining are approximately 2.8 percent per year lower than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment, and coal transportation rates in 2035 are between 25 and 27 percent higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: CAFE
cases.long_description: Assumes that LDV CAFE and greenhouse gas emissions standards proposed for model years 2017-2025 are enacted.

cases.title: High tech battery
cases.long_description: Significant improvement in vehicle battery and nonbattery system cost and performance.

cases.title: 2011 demand tech
cases.long_description: Future equipment purchases in the residential and commercial sectors are based only on the range of equipment available in 2011.  Energy efficiency of new industrial plant and equipment is held constant at the 2012 level over the projection period.

cases.title: High demand tech
cases.long_description: Earlier availability, lower costs, and higher efficiencies are applied to advanced residential and commercial equipment.  For new residential and commercial construction, building shell efficiencies are assumed to meet ENERGY STAR requirements after 2016.  Earlier availability, lower costs, and higher efficiency are applied to advanced industrial equipment and a more rapid rate of improvement is applied to the recovery of biomass byproducts from industrial processes.  The characteristics of conventional and alternative-fuel light-duty vehicles reflect more optimistic assumptions about incremental improvements in fuel economy and costs.  Freight trucks see more rapid improvement in fuel efficiency for engine and emissions control technologies.  More optimistic assumptions for fuel efficiency improvements are also made for the air, rail, and shipping sectors.

cases.title: Best building tech
cases.long_description: Future equipment purchases in the residential and commercial sectors are made from a menu of technologies that includes only the most efficient models available in a particular year for each fuel, regardless of cost.

cases.title: High EUR
cases.long_description: Estimated ultimate recovery per tight oil or shale gas well is 50 percent higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low EUR
cases.long_description: Estimated ultimate recovery per tight oil or shale gas well is 50 percent lower than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High TRR
cases.long_description: The well spacing for all tight oil and shale gas plays  is 8 wells per square mile (i.e., each well has an average drainage area of 80 acres), and the estimated ultimate recovery for tight oil and shale gas wells is 50 percent higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Reference 05
cases.long_description: Includes CSAPR and MATS as in the Reference case, with reduced 5-year environmental investment recovery.

cases.title: Low gas price 05
cases.description: 5-year investment recovery with low gas price
cases.long_description: Includes CSAPR and MATS as in the Reference case, with reduced 5-year environmental investment recovery combined with the High Estimated Ultimate Recovery case.

cases.title: $15 GHG
cases.long_description: Applies a fee for CO2 emissions throughout the economy, starting at $15 in 2013 and rising by 5 percent per year through 2035 (in 2010 dollars).  This fee is set to target the same reduction in CO2 emissions as in the AEO2011 GHG Price Economywide case.

cases.title: $25 GHG
cases.long_description: Applies a fee for CO2 emissions throughout the economy, starting at $25 in 2013 and rising by 5 percent per year through 2035 (in 2010 dollars).  This fee is set at the same dollar amount as in the AEO2011 GHG Price Economywide case.

cases.title: No GHG concern
cases.long_description: No GHG emissions reduction policy is enacted, and market investment decisions are not altered in anticipation of such a policy.

cases.title: Low tech
cases.long_description: Combination of the Integrated 2011 Demand Technology case with the assumption that costs of new power plants do not improve from 2012 levels throughout the projection.

cases.title: High tech
cases.long_description: Combines the Integrated High Demand Technology case and the Low Renewable Technology Cost case and also assumes that costs for new nuclear and fossil-fired power plants are lower than Reference case levels, by 20 percent in 2012 and 40 percent in 2035.

cases.title: Low renewable cost
cases.long_description: Costs for new nonhydropower renewable generating technologies start 20 percent lower in 2012 and decline to 40 percent lower than Reference case levels in 2035. Capital costs of renewable other liquid fuel technologies start 20 percent lower in 2012 and decline to approximately 40 percent lower than Reference case levels in 2035.

cases.title: Extended policies
cases.long_description: Begins with the No Sunset case but excludes extension of tax credits for blenders and for other biofuels that were included in the No Sunset case.   Assumes an increase in the capacity limitations on the ITC and extension of the program.  The case includes additional rounds of efficiency standards for residential and commercial products, as well as new standards for products not yet covered, adds multiple rounds of national building codes by 2026, and increases LDV fuel economy standards in the transportation sector to 62 miles per gallon in 2035.

cases.title: No sunset
cases.long_description: Assumes extension of all existing energy policies and legislation that contain sunset provisions, except those requiring additional funding (e.g., loan guarantee programs) and those that involve extensive regulatory analysis, such as CAFE improvements and periodic updates of efficiency standards.

cases.title: HDV NG reference
cases.description: Heavy duty vehicle natural gas reference
cases.long_description: Incorporates revised compressed natural gas and liquefied natural gas pricing assumptions and heavy-duty vehicle market acceptance.

cases.title: HDV NG potential
cases.description: Heavy duty vehicle natural gas potential
cases.long_description: Assumes expansion of natural gas refueling infrastructure for the heavy-duty vehicle market.

cases.long_description: Annual Energy Outlook 2012 Early release reference case released in December, 2011.

cases.title: Early release
cases.long_description: Preliminary reference case released on December 16, 2010.

cases.title: AEO2010 Reference
cases.long_description: Reference case from the AEO2010, featuring baseline economic growth (2.4 percent per year from 2008 through 2035), mid-range world oil prices, and baseline technology assumptions.

cases.title: High growth
cases.long_description: Real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 3.2 percent from 2009 to 2035. Other energy market assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low growth
cases.long_description: Real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 2.1 percent from 2009 to 2035.  Other energy market assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: High oil price
cases.long_description: More pessimistic assumptions for economic access to non-OPEC resources and for OPEC behavior than in the Reference case due to high non-OECD demand. World light, sweet crude oil prices are about $200 per barrel (2009 dollars) in 2035. OECD demand reacts to the price level.  Other assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low oil price
cases.long_description: More optimistic assumptions for economic access to non-OPEC resources and for OPEC behavior than in the Reference case due to low non-OECD demand. World light, sweet crude oil prices are $50 per barrel in 2035, compared with $125 per barrel in the Reference case (2009 dollars). OECD demand reacts to the price level.  Other assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: Traditional high oil price
cases.long_description: More pessimistic assumptions for economic access to non-OPEC resources and for OPEC behavior than in the Reference case with both OECD and non-OECD demand reacting to the price level. World light, sweet crude oil prices are about $200 per barrel (2009 dollars) in 2035.  Other assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: Traditional low oil price
cases.long_description: More optimistic assumptions for economic access to non-OPEC resources and for OPEC behavior than in the Reference case with both OECD and non-OECD demand reacting to the price level. World light, sweet crude oil prices are $50 per barrel in 2035, compared with $125 per barrel in the Reference case (2009 dollars). Other assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: High technology
cases.long_description: Combination of the Residential, Commercial, Industrial, and Transportation High Technology cases and the Electricity Low Fossil Technology Cost, Low Renewable Technology Cost, and Low Nuclear Cost cases.

cases.title: Low technology
cases.long_description: Combination of the Residential, Commercial, and Industrial 2010 Technology cases and the Electricity High Fossil Technology Cost, High Renewable Technology Cost, and High Nuclear Cost cases.

cases.title: High coal cost
cases.long_description: Productivity growth rates for coal mining are lower than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment costs, other mine supply costs, and coal transportation rates are higher.

cases.title: Low coal cost
cases.long_description: Productivity growth rates for coal mining are higher than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment costs, other mine supply costs, and coal transportation rates are lower.

cases.title: High fossil cost
cases.long_description: Costs for new advanced fossil-fired generating technologies do not improve due to learning over time from 2011.

cases.title: Low fossil cost
cases.long_description: Capital and operating costs for all new fossil-fired generating technologies start 20 percent below the Reference case and decline to 40 percent below the Reference case in 2035.

cases.title: High nuclear cost
cases.long_description: Costs for new nuclear technology do not improve due to learning from 2011 levels in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low nuclear cost
cases.long_description: Capital and operating costs for new nuclear capacity start 20 percent below the Reference case and decline to 40 percent below the Reference case in 2035.

cases.title: Frozen costs
cases.long_description: Base overnight costs for all new electricity generating technology are frozen at 2015 levels.  Cost decreases due to learning can still occur.

cases.title: Decreasing costs
cases.long_description: Base overnight costs for all new electricity generating technologies are assumed to be 20 percent below the Reference case through a reduction in the annual cost index, and decline more rapidly so that the cost index is 40 percentage points below the Reference case in 2035.

cases.title: High renewable cost
cases.long_description: Capital costs, operating and maintenance costs, and performance levels for wind, biomass, and geothermal resources do not improve due to learning from 2011 levels in the Reference case.  Dedicated energy crops do not become available.

cases.title: Low renewable cost
cases.long_description: Levelized costs of energy resources for nonhydropower renewable generating technologies start 20 percent below the Reference case in 2011 and decline to 40 percent below the Reference case in 2035.  Biomass fuel supplies are 40 percent less expensive than in the Reference case.  The rate of improvement in recovery of biomass byproducts from industrial processes is increased.

cases.title: No GHG concern
cases.long_description: No greenhouse gas emissions reduction policy is enacted, and market investment decisions are not altered in anticipation of such a policy.

cases.title: Extended policies
cases.long_description: Begins with the Reference case and selectively extends PTC, ITC, and other energy efficiency tax credit policies with sunset provisions, and promulgates new efficiency standards as they satisfy the EERE consumer-related cost-effectiveness criteria.  Increases light duty vehicle fuel economy standards by 3 percent per year for model years 2017 through 2025.  Industrial combined heat and power tax credits were expanded to cover all system sizes and increased to $25,000.

cases.title: Low EOR - GHG price
cases.long_description: Availability of carbon dioxide from plants converting coal and/or biomass to liquid fuels is reduced and a carbon fee exists, set at the level of the cost containment provision as specified in both the American Power Act of 2010 and the American Clean Energy and Security Act of 2009.

cases.title: Low EOR
cases.long_description: Availability of carbon dioxide from plants converting coal and/or biomass to liquid fuels is reduced by 50 percent from the Reference case.

cases.title: GHG price
cases.long_description: Carbon allowance fee is set at the level of the cost containment provision as specified in both the American Power Act of 2010 and the American Clean Energy and Security Act of 2009.

cases.title: "Retrofit 5, low gas price"
cases.long_description: All coal-fired utility boilers must install flue-gas desulfurization scrubbers by 2020 to comply with acid gas reduction requirements, and implement selective catalytic reduction to meet future nitrogen oxide and ozone requirements, or be retired if not economic.  Investments are recovered over 5 years.  Availability of shale gas is increased by applying the assumptions of the High Shale EUR case.

cases.title: "Retrofit 20, low gas price"
cases.long_description: All coal-fired utility boilers must install flue-gas desulfurization scrubbers by 2020 to comply with acid gas reduction requirements, and implement selective catalytic reduction to meet future nitrogen oxide and ozone requirements, or be retired if not economic.  Investments are recovered over 20 years.  Availability of shale gas is increased by applying the assumptions of the High Shale EUR case.

cases.title: Retrofit 5
cases.long_description: All coal-fired utility boilers must install flue-gas desulfurization scrubbers by 2020 to comply with acid gas reduction requirements, and implement selective catalytic reduction to meet future nitrogen oxide and ozone requirements, or be retired if not economic.  Investments are recovered over 5 years.

cases.title: Retrofit 20
cases.long_description: All coal-fired utility boilers must install flue-gas desulfurization scrubbers by 2020 to comply with acid gas reduction requirements, and implement selective catalytic reduction to meet future nitrogen oxide and ozone requirements, or be retired if not economic.  Investments are recovered over 20 years.

cases.title: Transport mercury MACT 5
cases.long_description: The Air Transport Rule limits on sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides and a 90-percent mercury Maximum Achievable Control Technology are enacted with a 5 year investment recovery period.

cases.title: Transport mercury MACT 20
cases.long_description: The Air Transport Rule limits on sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides and a 90-percent mercury Maximum Achievable Control Technology are enacted with a 20 year investment recovery period.

cases.title: High OCS resource
cases.long_description: Oil and natural gas resources in undeveloped areas of the Outer Continental Shelf are assumed to be 3 times higher than in the Reference case by tripling the size of the fields.

cases.title: High OCS costs
cases.long_description: The costs of exploration and development of oil and natural gas resources in the lower 48 Outer Continental Shelf are 30 percent higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: OCS access
cases.long_description: No new lease sales occur in the Outer Continental Shelf region of the Eastern Gulf of Mexico, Pacific Ocean, or Atlantic Ocean through 2035.

cases.title: High E15
cases.long_description: E15 restrictions will be removed in all states by 2015, and E15 penetration rises to 99 percent of the potential maximum level in all regions by 2020.

cases.title: Low E15
cases.long_description: The penetration of E15 in all demand regions is slower than in the Reference case, reaching a lower maximum level.

cases.title: HDV fuel economy standard
cases.long_description: Fuel economy simulates the expected fuel economy impact of the Environmental Protection Agency's and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's proposed fuel economy standards for model years 2014 through 2018 for Class 2b through Class 8 heavy duty vehicles.

cases.title: 6% LDV fuel economy growth
cases.long_description: Fuel economy standards are increased by 6 percent per year for model years 2017 through 2025, and are held constant from 2026 through 2035.

cases.title: 3% LDV fuel economy growth
cases.long_description: Fuel economy standards are increased by 3 percent per year for model years 2017 through 2025, and are held constant from 2026 through 2035.

cases.title: Slow oil/gas technology
cases.long_description: Improvements in exploration and development costs, production rates, and success rates due to technological advancement are reduced by 50 percent to reflect slower improvement than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Rapid oil/gas technology
cases.long_description: Improvements in exploration and development costs, production rates, and success rates due to technological advancement are increased by 50 percent to reflect more rapid improvement than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High shale recovery per well
cases.long_description: The total unproved technically recoverable shale gas resources are increased from 827 trillion cubic feet in the Reference case to 1,230 trillion cubic feet.  The estimated ultimate recovery per shale gas well is 50 percent higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High shale recovery per play
cases.long_description: The total unproved technically recoverable shale gas resources are increased from 827 trillion cubic feet in the Reference case to 1,230 trillion cubic feet.  The recovery rate per well is unchanged from the Reference case, resulting in more wells needed to recover the shale gas in each play.

cases.title: Low shale recovery per play
cases.long_description: The total unproved technically recoverable  shale gas resources are reduced from 827 trillion cubic feet in the Reference case to 423 trillion cubic feet. cases.title: Reference
cases.long_description: A policy-neutral reference case very similar to the AEO2010 Reference case, but with results differing slightly due to model changes to represent the APA, such as emission coverage definitions and incentive programs.

cases.title: Reference High Nat. Gas
cases.description: Alternate reference case with high natural gas resources
cases.long_description: An alternative policy-neutral reference case where natural gas resources from shale in the onshore, lower-48 states are assumed to be higher than in the standard Reference case.  This alternative reference case is provided for comparison to the APA High Natural Gas Resource case.

cases.title: Basic
cases.long_description: An APA case with Reference-case assumptions about technology costs and availability.  Key low-emission technologies are available on a large scale consistent with the emissions reduction requirements of APA.  The use of offsets, both domestic and international, is not instantaneous but is also not severely constrained by cost, regulation, or the pace of negotiations with key countries.  Covered entities and investors are assumed to amass an aggregate allowance bank of approximately 10 gigatonnes by 2035 through a combination of offset usage and emission reductions that exceed the level required under the emission caps

cases.title: Zero Bank
cases.long_description: Similar to the APA Basic case with no banked allowances held in 2035, reflecting the assumed availability after 2035 of a broad array of reasonably priced low- and no-carbon technologies that diminishes the market incentives for holding substantial allowance balance beyond 2035.

cases.title: High Nat. Gas
cases.long_description: Similar to the APA Basic case, but with natural gas resources from shale in the onshore, lower-48 states are assumed to be higher.

cases.title: High cost
cases.long_description: Similar to the APA Basic case, but assumed overnight capital costs of nuclear, fossil with carbon capture and storage, and dedicated biomass are 50 percent higher. Covered entities are also assumed to amass an aggregate 12-gigatonne allowance bank by 2035.

cases.title: No Int'l
cases.long_description: Similar to the APA Basic case, but represents an extreme where the use of international offsets is eliminated by cost, regulation, and/or slow progress in reaching international agreements or arrangements covering offsets in key countries and sectors.  Covered entities are assumed to amass an aggregate 12-gigatonne allowance bank by 2035 in this case.

cases.title: Limited / No Int'l
cases.description: APA No international offsets / Limited alternatives
cases.long_description: Similar to the APA Basic case, but with international offset use eliminated and nuclear, fossil with carbon capture and storage, and dedicated biomass technologies are limited to Reference case levels. The extreme assumed limits on many of the key emissions reduction options in this case make compliance extremely challenging and lead to rapid shifts in the remaining alternatives that may be difficult to achieve. This should be kept in mind when reviewing the results in this case.

cases.long_description: Baseline economic growth (2.4 percent per year from 2008 through 2035), world oil price, and technology assumptions.

cases.title: High growth
cases.long_description: Real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 3.0 percent from 2008 to 2035. Other energy market assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low growth
cases.long_description: Real GDP grows at an average annual rate of 1.8 percent from 2008 to 2035.  Other energy market assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: High technology
cases.long_description: Combination of the Residential, Commercial, Industrial, and Transportation High Technology cases and the Electricity Low Fossil Technology Cost, Low Renewable Technology Cost, and Low Nuclear Cost cases.

cases.title: Low technology
cases.long_description: Combination of the Residential, Commercial, and Industrial 2010 Technology cases and the Electricity High Fossil Technology Cost, High Renewable Technology Cost, and High Nuclear Cost cases.

cases.title: High coal cost
cases.long_description: Productivity growth rates for coal mining are lower than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment, and coal transportation rates are higher. Partial projection tables in Appendix D

cases.title: Low coal cost
cases.long_description: Productivity growth rates for coal mining are higher than in the Reference case, and coal mining wages, mine equipment, and coal transportation rates are lower.

cases.title: High fossil cost
cases.long_description: Costs for new advanced fossil-fired generating technologies do not improve due to learning over time from 2010.

cases.title: Low fossil cost
cases.long_description: Capital and operating costs for all new fossil-fired generating technologies start 10 percent below the Reference case and decline to 25 percent below the Reference case in 2035.

cases.title: High nuclear cost
cases.long_description: Costs for new nuclear technology do not improve due to learning from 2010 levels in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low nuclear cost
cases.long_description: Capital and operating costs for new nuclear capacity start 10 percent below the Reference case and decline to 25 percent below the Reference case in 2035.

cases.title: High renewable cost
cases.long_description: New renewable generating technologies do not improve through learning over time from 2010.

cases.title: Low renewable cost
cases.long_description: Levelized cost of energy for nonhydropower renewable generating technologies start 10 percent below the Reference case in 2010 and decline to 25 percent below the Reference case in 2035.

cases.title: Rapid oil/gas technology
cases.long_description: Improvements in exploration and development costs, production rates, and success rates due to technological advancement are increased by 50 percent to reflect more rapid improvement than in the Reference case.

cases.title: Slow oil/gas technology
cases.long_description: Improvements in exploration and development costs, production rates, and success rates due to technological advancement are reduced by 50 percent to reflect slower improvement than in the Reference case.

cases.title: High oil price
cases.long_description: More pessimistic assumptions for economic access to non-OPEC resources and for OPEC behavior than in the Reference case. World light, sweet crude oil prices are about $210 per barrel (2008 dollars) in 2035. Other assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: Low oil price
cases.long_description: More optimistic assumptions for economic access to non-OPEC resources and for OPEC behavior than in the Reference case. World light, sweet crude oil prices are $51 per barrel in 2035, compared with $133 per barrel in the Reference case (2008 dollars). Other assumptions are the same as in the Reference case.

cases.title: High shale gas
cases.long_description: Shale gas resources in the onshore, lower 48 are assumed to be higher than in the Reference case.

cases.title: No shale gas
cases.description: No new shale gas drilling after 2009
cases.long_description: No drilling is permitted in onshore, lower 48 shale gas reservoirs after 2009 (i.e., no new shale gas drilling).

cases.title: No shale/tight sands
cases.description: No new tight gas and shale drilling after 2009
cases.long_description: No drilling is permitted in onshore, lower 48 low-permeability natural gas reservoirs after 2009 (i.e., no new tight gas or shale gas drilling).

cases.title: 2019 phaseout
cases.long_description: Modified Reference case incorporating lower incremental costs for all classes of heavy-duty natural gas vehicles and tax incentives for natural gas refueling stations and natural gas fuel beginning in 2011 and phased out by 2019.

cases.title: 2027 phaseout
cases.long_description: Modified Reference case incorporating lower incremental costs for all classes of heavy-duty natural gas vehicles and tax incentives for natural gas refueling stations and natural gas fuel beginning in 2011 and phased out by 2027, with assumed increases in 2035 market shares for all classes of heavy-duty natural gas vehicles.

cases.title: Low price/2019 phaseout
cases.description: Low oil price with 2019 phaseout with base market potential
cases.long_description: Modified Low Oil Price case incorporating lower incremental costs for all classes of heavy-duty natural gas vehicles and tax incentives for natural gas refueling stations and natural gas fuel beginning in 2011 and phased out by 2019.

cases.title: Low price/2027 phaseout
cases.description: Low oil price with 2027 phaseout with expanded market potential
cases.long_description: Modified Low Oil Price case incorporating lower incremental costs for all classes of heavy-duty natural gas vehicles and tax incentives for natural gas refueling stations and natural gas fuel beginning in 2011 and phased out by 2027, with assumed increases in 2035 market shares for all classes of heavy-duty natural gas vehicles.

cases.title: Nuclear retirement
cases.long_description: All existing nuclear plants are retired after 60 years of operation.

cases.title: No GHG concern
cases.long_description: No greenhouse gas emissions reduction policy is enacted, and market investment decisions are not altered in anticipation of such a policy.

cases.title: High LNG
cases.long_description: LNG imports into North America are set exogenously to a factor times the levels projected in the Reference case from 2010 forward. The factor starts at 1.0 in 2010 and increases linearly to 5.0 in 2035.

cases.title: No sunset
cases.long_description: Begins with the Reference case and extends all energy policies and legislation with sunset provisions, except those requiring additional funding (e.g., loan guarantee programs).  Also extends the RFS requirement to 36 billion gallons by 2026 and continues increasing proportional to transport demand thereafter.

cases.title: Extended policies
cases.long_description: Begins with the Reference case and selectively extends PTC, ITC, and other energy efficiency tax credit policies with sunset provisions, and promulgates new efficiency standards as they satisfy the EERE consumer-related cost-effectiveness criteria.  Introduces new CAFE and tailpipe emissions proposal.

cases.title: Updated AEO2009 reference
cases.long_description: AEO2009 reference case updated to include the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act enacted in February 2009 and revisions to the macroeconomic outlook.
